subject: geography
title: Tectonic Hazards Adventure: Case Studies
welcome_lead: Tohoku vs Haiti — why do similar quakes have such different impacts? Time for case studies.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography Tectonic Hazards case studies — Tohoku 2011, Haiti 2010, HIC vs LIC.
final_note: You compared a HIC and LIC earthquake and learned about monitoring, prediction and planning.

concepts.def: Damage caused directly by the shaking itself
High Income Country — wealthy, resilient infrastructure
Low Income Country — fewer resources for response
Building codes, drills, hazard maps to reduce risk

walkthroughs.body_html:
Magnitude 9.0 quake offshore triggered a 40m tsunami.

Around 15,900 deaths — mostly from the tsunami, not the shaking. Earthquake-resistant buildings saved thousands. The Fukushima nuclear meltdown was a secondary effect.

Magnitude 7.0 quake near Port-au-Prince — far smaller than Tohoku.

Yet around 230,000 deaths. Poor building quality, no early warning, weak emergency response. A cholera outbreak followed — a deadly secondary effect.

Monitoring: seismometers track tremors; GPS tracks plate movement.

Protection: cross-bracing, base isolators, deep foundations.

Preparation: drills (Japan's Disaster Prevention Day), hazard maps, emergency kits.

mcqs.q: Which is a SECONDARY effect of the 2011 Tohoku earthquake?
Why did Haiti 2010 cause far more deaths than Tohoku 2011 despite being a smaller quake?
options: Haiti was closer to the equator
Poor building quality and weak response in an LIC

numericals.q: Approximately how many people died in the 2010 Haiti earthquake (thousands)?
numericals.hint: Around a quarter of a million — devastating for an LIC capital.
